keys.title: Security keys
keys.hint: Unlock {app} with a FIDO2 key (YubiKey, Nitrokey, SoloKey…) and its PIN. The secret is computed by the key itself: nothing is stored in the system keychain. Register a second key as a backup; the master password stays valid.

wizard.title: Add a security key
wizard.plugInHint: YubiKey, Nitrokey, SoloKey… into a USB port. It will be detected automatically.
wizard.multipleHint: Leave only the one to register.
wizard.unsupportedHint: A FIDO2 key with a PIN and the hmac-secret extension is required. Older U2F-only keys are not enough.
wizard.noPin: This key has no PIN yet: it is required, let's create it.
wizard.keepPlugged: Keep the key plugged in until the end. Only touch it when {app} asks you to: a touch at another time can type a code into the active window.
wizard.pinIntro.before: The PIN protects the key: without it, someone who found it could not open your vault. It is stored
wizard.pinIntro.after: and will also be used by other sites and applications that use it.
wizard.pinHint: {count} characters minimum; digits, letters or both.
wizard.pinMismatch: The two PINs do not match.
wizard.keyNameHint: To recognize it in the list, for example “Blue YubiKey”.
wizard.passwordHint: To confirm that it is really you adding this key.
wizard.touch1: It blinks: touch it to create the credential.
wizard.touch2: It blinks again: touch it a second time to finish.
wizard.registeredHint: It can now unlock the vault.
wizard.tryIt: To try it: lock with {keys}, choose “Use a security key”, enter the PIN then touch the key.
wizard.backupAdvice: Remember to also register a backup key, in case this one is lost.
wizard.timeoutNote: Without a touch, the key gives up on its own after about 30 seconds.
oidc.pocket.before1: In Pocket ID: Administration → OIDC Clients → Add, name “Quayline”.
oidc.pocket.after1: Check “Public client” and “PKCE”, save, then copy the Client ID below.
oidc.pocket.phone: Offered automatically with Pocket ID 0.50 or later.
oidc.authentik.issuerHint: The issuer address (“OpenID Configuration Issuer”) shown by the provider.
oidc.authentik.before1: In Authentik: Applications → Applications → “Create with provider”, provider “OAuth2/OpenID”.
oidc.authentik.after1: Copy the Client ID, and the provider's “OpenID Configuration Issuer” address (it ends with the application's “slug”).
oidc.authentik.after2: Groups are sent with the “profile” scope.
oidc.authentik.phone: To enable in System → Brands → “Device code” flow.
oidc.authelia.before1: In Authelia's configuration (identity_providers → oidc → clients), add a client: client_id of your choice, public: true, require_pkce: true, pkce_challenge_method: S256.
oidc.authelia.after1: scopes: openid, profile, groups. Restart Authelia, then enter the client_id below.
oidc.authelia.phone: Offered automatically if your Authelia version supports it.
oidc.keycloak.before1: In the Keycloak console, choose the realm, then Clients → Create client (OpenID Connect), Client ID of your choice.
oidc.keycloak.before2: “Client authentication” off (public client), “Standard flow” checked; also check “OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant” for the QR code.
oidc.keycloak.after1: Groups: Client scopes → <client>-dedicated → Configure a new mapper → Group Membership, “Token Claim Name”: groups, “Add to ID token” checked.
oidc.keycloak.after2: In Advanced → “Proof Key for Code Exchange Code Challenge Method”: S256.
oidc.keycloak.phone: Offered if “OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant” is checked on the client.
oidc.entra.issuerHint: Replace <tenant ID> with the directory ID (GUID) shown on the application page.
oidc.entra.groupHint: Entra sends groups by their ID, not by their name.
oidc.entra.before1: Entra portal: Applications → App registrations → New registration, “Accounts in this organizational directory only”.
oidc.entra.after1: Authentication: “Allow public client flows” set to Yes (needed for the QR code).
oidc.entra.after2: To require a group: Token configuration → Add groups claim.
oidc.entra.after3: Copy the Application (client) ID below, and the Directory (tenant) ID into the address.
oidc.entra.phone: Offered; may be blocked by a Conditional Access policy.
oidc.google.before1: Google Cloud Console: APIs & Services → Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID, type “Desktop app”.
oidc.google.redirect: Nothing to declare for the redirect URL, Google accepts local addresses automatically. Quayline will use:
oidc.google.after1: Copy the client ID and client secret: Google requires it, but it is not confidential for a desktop application.
oidc.google.after2: No groups at Google: only the account used at activation will be able to unlock.
oidc.google.phone: Not available: Google reserves it for another client type.
oidc.generic.issuerHint: The address whose “/.well-known/openid-configuration” gives the configuration.
oidc.generic.groupHint: Add the scope that sends groups, if needed.
oidc.generic.before1: Create a public OpenID Connect client, with PKCE (S256).
oidc.generic.phone: Offered automatically if the provider announces it.
